sentences.text: A cabinet outage is treated as a service incident when the cabinet stops responding, reports a fault, or fails a dispensing check.
The IT Operations Specialist uses the Cabinet Downtime Notice to open a controlled incident record and identify the affected cabinet.
The IT Operations Specialist checks controller status, network connectivity, and recent event logs before attempting recovery.
The IT Operations Specialist records the time the fault was detected and the affected equipment identifier.
The affected North Ward Cabinet Controller or South Ward Cabinet Controller remains Out of Service while the cause is assessed.
The IT Operations Specialist isolates the fault where necessary to prevent repeated dispense requests from reaching an unavailable cabinet.
The Medication Order Gateway retains pending requests for review rather than treating an interrupted transaction as completed.
The IT Operations Specialist checks whether any transaction was interrupted before the cabinet became unavailable.
The Pharmacy Verification Station is used to confirm that pending medication orders remain valid before they are re-presented.
The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot is held from supplying medication to a cabinet that has not passed its recovery checks.
The IT Operations Specialist coordinates technical troubleshooting with the Biomedical Engineer when equipment inspection or repair is required.
The Clinical Pharmacist reviews medication orders affected by the outage when clinical validation is needed.
The Registered Nurse uses the established clinical process for urgent medication needs while the cabinet is unavailable.
The Biomedical Engineer reports completed repairs and any equipment limitations to the IT Operations Specialist.
After repair, the IT Operations Specialist verifies communications, status reporting, and cabinet transaction behavior under controlled conditions.
The responsible staff confirm that no unresolved transaction could cause a duplicate or missed dispense.
The cabinet remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return to Ready for Dispense.
The West Tube Dispatch Console uses the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record to verify capsule identity and seal status before closing its dispatch-side handoff checks.
The West Tube Dispatch Console records completion of its handoff checks only after the required dispatch data are consistent.
The Pneumatic Tube Network remains under monitoring while dispatch service is being restored.
The Hospital Courier confirms physical receipt through the established delivery process.
The West Tube Dispatch Console retains the handoff completion status for operational review.
The IT Operations Specialist monitors cabinet and tube service status for recurrence during the recovery period.
Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, recovery checks, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.
